Un modèle qui repère bien les personnes,: Does a model that finds people, companies and products reliably in Wikipedia still find them in tweets? We measured the drop, then looked for where it came from.
Le sujet imposé était de reconnaître des: The assigned topic was to recognise people, companies and products in text, starting from a published research project: Linked-DocRED (SIGIR 2023). It is built on about 5,000 Wikipedia documents and chains four modules: name detection, grouping mentions of the same entity, relations between entities, and linking to Wikidata.
Après la première séance, l’encadrant no: After the first session, our supervisor asked us to focus on name recognition. The question became: does a model trained on well-written articles stay reliable on short, informal messages?
: le code publié ne fonctionnait pas en: : the published code did not run as released. I set up one isolated environment per module (three Python versions under WSL2) and fixed the blocking bugs: a hidden 10-document limit, a test that actually used the validation data, a call to the wrong API, and unpinned dependencies. I also adapted training to fit on an 8 GB GPU.
: le script d’évaluation publié ne notai: : the published evaluation script only scored the last document and gave a perfect score to nonsensical predictions. I wrote a corrected version.
: revue des travaux qui citent l’article: : review of the papers citing the original work and a selection grid for datasets.
: exécution de toutes les expériences GP: : ran all the end-of-project GPU experiments on Google Colab (a model over three random seeds, a test on an additional corpus, preprocessing variants).
: présentation de mi-parcours en anglais: : mid-term presentation in English and writing the reproduction section of the paper.
La conception des modèles et l’essentiel: Model design and most of the error analysis were led by a teammate.
Quatre jeux de données aux étiquettes di: Four datasets with different labels were mapped to a common scheme: person, company, product, other. Four families of models were compared: a classic CRF, RoBERTa trained on our data, GLiNER used without training, and a large language model (Llama) prompted with a few examples. All are scored on the same sentences with the same metric, and the test set is only used at the end.

Le meilleur modèle entraîné uniquement s: The best model trained only on Wikipedia-style text drops from 0.835 to 0.375 on tweets. When also trained on tweets, it reaches 0.73.
Les balises propres à Twitter expliquent: Twitter-specific markup explains about a third of the drop: removing it gains 0.16 for a model that has never seen tweets, but costs 0.05 for a model that has learned them.
À la relecture, 26 à 44 % des « erreurs: On review, 26 to 44% of the model’s “errors” were judged correct by two reviewers: part of the drop comes from ambiguous annotations, not from the model.

Le jeu de données est le jeu Rock Paper: The dataset is the Rock Paper Scissors set published by TensorFlow, with a training set and a separate test set. The three classes are balanced. Images are resized to 128 × 128 pixels and normalised.
Beaucoup d'images ont des fonds homogène: Many images have plain backgrounds and even lighting, much simpler than a real webcam. To narrow that gap, every training image goes through random transformations: flips, rotations up to 20°, colour and brightness changes, shifts and zoom, conversion to greyscale, and masking of a region.
: quatre blocs de convolution (de 32 à 2: : four convolution blocks (32 to 256 filters) with normalisation and dropout, followed by a three-output classifier. About 1.2 million parameters, trained from scratch.
: un réseau léger déjà entraîné sur Imag: : a lightweight network already trained on ImageNet, with its last layer replaced. Training happens in two steps: first the new layer alone, then the last five blocks with a very small learning rate.
Les deux modèles suivent le même protoco: Both models follow the same protocol: 90% of the training images for learning, 10% for validation, the test set kept for the final evaluation, a fixed random seed, learning-rate reduction and early stopping when validation stops improving.

sur l'ensemble de test, devant MobileNet: on the test set, ahead of MobileNetV2. On images this simple and this specific, a smaller model trained directly on the data did better than the pre-trained one. The best model is selected automatically and saved with its class mapping, so it can be reloaded without retraining.
: MediaPipe Hands localise la main dans: : MediaPipe Hands locates the hand in the webcam image and finds the finger joints.
: la position des articulations indique: : the position of the joints shows which fingers are open or closed.
: les prédictions des dernières images s: : predictions from the last few frames are kept and the most frequent one is used, so the result does not flicker from frame to frame.
: une interface avec écran de démarrage: : an interface with a start screen shows the detected gesture, the computer's move, the score and the result of each round.
: une fonction analyse aussi une seule i: : a function also analyses one image and displays the model's confidence for each class, which helps when studying errors.
Les erreurs apparaissent surtout quand l: Errors mostly appear when lighting is poor, the hand is partly out of frame, the gesture is badly formed or the background is cluttered.
Le jeu de données manque de diversité :: The dataset lacks diversity: few different hands, angles and lighting conditions.
Le système ne connaît que trois gestes :: The system only knows three gestures: adding more requires new data and retraining.
Pistes : un jeu de données plus varié, u: Next steps: a more varied dataset, systematic hand detection before classification, and a lighter model for low-powered machines.
Un modèle pré-entraîné n'est pas meilleu: A pre-trained model is not better by default: it has to be compared with a simpler solution, using the same protocol, before choosing it.
Un bon score sur le jeu de test ne suffi: A good test score is not enough either: with a real webcam, lighting and background matter as much as the model.

sur le C2, qui accepte n'importe quel so: on the C2, which accepts any subdomain and logs every query received, so the exfiltrated data can be reassembled.

Un premier tunnel DNS « naïf » (données: A first "naive" DNS tunnel (data hex-encoded in subdomains) triggers the custom rules: the C2 domain and the length of the labels give the exfiltration away.
: de simples variations d'écriture de la: : simple changes to how the request is written (URL encoding) keep the attack while slipping past the signatures.
: une version furtive du tunnel remplace: : a stealthy version of the tunnel replaces hex with Base32, adds a random prefix to each label and spaces out the queries randomly. The traffic then looks like ordinary DNS.
